name: sdrift-stdnum-stdnum-003-shared
instr:
# Align python-stdnum with its documented contract

The repository at `/app` is `python-stdnum` — a library of routines for parsing, validating and formatting international standard numbers and identifiers. Its intended behaviour is defined by its own
documentation: the prose documentation under `/app/docs/` and the module and function docstrings under `/app/stdnum/`. Right now the implementation and the documentation disagree; the code runs,
but at certain inputs it returns something the documentation says it should not.

Your task: study the documented behaviour, compare it to the code, and change the implementation so it
matches the documentation wherever the two disagree. Keep the public API, signatures and file layout
exactly as they are, edit only files under `/app/stdnum/`, and add no new files. There is no network
access. Correctness is measured by replaying held-out inputs (compact/validate operations and documented helper predicates over international identifiers) against the documented
behaviour, so align to the documentation itself rather than to any particular test.

Before editing, write a short plan to /app/NOTES.md — what the docs specify, where the code diverges, and how you'll verify your fix — then implement it.
